maria_support: ACME reports a p99 jump from ~350ms -> 2.1s on /v1/completions (acme-prod) starting ~08:30 UTC. They also saw a couple of 504s. Customer says traffic unchanged.

lina_sre: Thanks Maria — can you paste a sample request ID? we can check routing + node logs. Also any recent deploys? :eyes:

maria_support: sample request_id=req_20240316_acme_7f9a, tenant=acme-prod. No user-facing deploys on their side. We did a config rollout at 08:20 for autoscaler policy across prod-region but that was a control-plane-only change (no runtime binary).

ashok_runtime: grabbing logs. Running quick grep: `rtdb logs --tenant acme-prod --since 2h | grep req_20240316_acme_7f9a -A50` shows long GC pauses and repeated "alloc failed: slab exhaustion" traces around 08:31. Also see repeated KV-growth warnings: `kv_cache: entries=1.9M -> 2.8M` in 10m.

lina_sre: KV growth + slab exhaustion => likely fragmentation driving OOM/backpressure, which explains p95/p99 tail spikes even if throughput nominal. Any tenant with large prefix caching or runaway sessions?

maria_support: ACME runs a high-concurrency chat (many long contexts). They enabled prefix caching a week ago for cost savings.

ashok_runtime: Repro steps we used: 1) hit endpoint with long-context synthetic load (~4k tokens, concurrency 40) 2) observe heap growth, fragmentation, and rising p99. Confirmed locally on a 48GB GPU instance. Command used: ```ab -n 1000 -c 40 -p long_payload.json -T application/json https://runtime.prod/v1/completions```

lina_sre: Immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) temporarily disable prefix caching for acme-prod (config flag `prefix_cache.enabled=false` on tenant config) 2) cap concurrency for tenant -> set `max_concurrent_sequences=16` 3) trigger a rolling restart of runtime pods serving that tenant (to reclaim fragmented GPU slabs). Any objections?

maria_support: I can push config change and cap now. Customer approved a brief restart window.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: tenant-config/acme-prod update prefix_cache=false (deploy_id=dpl_789). Rolling restart scheduled for runtime-prod-ss (maxUnavailable=1).

ashok_runtime: After disabling prefix cache and restart, we saw KV entries drop back to ~600k and slab alloc failures stop. p99 improved to ~420ms within ~5 mins. Logs: `kv_cache: entries=2.8M -> 610k`, `allocator: fragmentation_ratio 0.72 -> 0.26`.

lina_sre: Longer-term fixes: - tune slab size thresholds and enable slab defrag heuristics (`RT_ALLOC_SLAB_DEFRAG=1`) - add eviction hysteresis for KV cache (soft_limit + aggressive eviction when slab fragmentation >0.6) - enhance telemetry to emit per-tenant slab fragmentation metric (for earlier alerts).

ashok_runtime: Also looking at allocator changes: reducing per-sequence max_kv_reserve and introducing a cap on per-tenant cached KV memory. We'll open an RFC and patch the runtime: change default slab bucket growth factor from 1.5 -> 1.25 and add `tenant_kv_max_bytes` enforcement.

maria_support: Customer reports latency normalized and 504s stopped. They've requested a postmortem and confirmation of permanent mitigations. I told them we'll follow up with a summary and timeline.

lina_sre: I'll create a short incident note and follow-up action items: 1) telemetry alert for fragmentation_ratio > 0.5 per tenant 2) runtime patch RFC + canary 3) ops playbook: disable prefix cache + cap concurrency + restart if slab exhaustion detected.

maria_support: tagging acme contact and scheduling postmortem sync for tomorrow. Thanks team :thumbsup:

ashok_runtime: For the record, repro artifacts and logs: `/mnt/ci/artifacts/acme-prod/1745554321/` contains `ab_long_payload.json`, `runtime_stdout.log`, and `alloc-trace-08-31.txt`. I'll attach to the RFC.

lina_sre: closing thread here but will link incident in #postmortems when PM doc is ready.

maria_support: resolved for now — will reopen if anything else crops up.
